src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implement the domain's ProductRepository and OrderRepository, so the module uses the domain's abstractions consistently

parsedVerdict.reasoning: All three files serve one concern: the outer layer of the fulfilment app. http-server.ts is the HTTP adapter, in-memory-repositories.ts holds the in-memory stores and server.ts wires them together and starts the server. The repositories implement the domain's ProductRepository and OrderRepository interfaces. The HTTP layer goes only through FulfilmentService and never calls the repositories directly, so the module does not bypass its own abstractions. However, http-server.ts repeats the order-state check in two places. The GET /orders and PATCH /orders/:id/state handlers each contain the same `orderStates.includes(state as OrderState)` check and the same error message. That message hard-codes the state list ("placed, paid, packed, shipped, delivered"), which the domain already defines once as `orderStates`. One rule therefore lives in several places, and the message will go stale if the domain's states change. This fails the rubric's rule that each invariant lives in one place. The issue is small, so confidence is moderate.

violations.message: The order-state check is written twice, in the GET /orders and PATCH /orders/:id/state handlers. Both copies hard-code the list of states in the error message instead of building it from the domain's `orderStates`. One rule therefore lives in several places, and the message will go stale if the domain's order states change. Move it into one shared parse/validate helper that builds the message from `orderStates`.
